raw_segments.text: What most struck the poor monk was the fact that in spite of his strict fasting and great age
Father Farrapont still looked a vigorous old man. He was tall, held himself erect, and had a thin but fresh and healthy face.
There was no doubt he still had considerable strength. He was of athletic build. In spite of his great age
he was not even quite gray and still had very thick hair and a full beard, both of which had once been black.
His eyes were gray, large and luminous, but strikingly prominent.
He spoke with a broad accent.
He was dressed in a peasant's long reddish coat of coarse convict cloth, as it used to be called, and had a stout rope
round his waist. His throat and chest were bare.
Beneath his coat, his shirt of the corsest linen showed almost black with dirt, not having been changed for months.
They said that he wore irons weighing 30 pounds under his coat.
His stockingless feet were thrust in old slippers, almost dropping to pieces.
